Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] ChatGPT share-link to openew[.]app navigation chain (LLMShare lure) · [LLM] Browser download from openew[.]app or pinned LLMShare hosting IPs · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] LLMShare anti-VM discovery: WMI BIOS/Computer queries + HKLM\HARDWARE reads post-installer launch · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Execution of LLMShare ChatGPT-installer SHA256 (Windows / macOS) · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
[LLM] ChatGPT share-link to openew[.]app navigation chain (LLMShare lure) Delivery High
Hunts the campaign-defining browser navigation pattern: a user lands on chatgpt.com/s/ (a ChatGPT shared-page URL) and within the same browser session navigates to openew[.]app — the off-platform fake OpenAI download portal. The chatgpt.com/s/ rendering feature is the lure surface; openew[.]app is the payload host. Rationale: Anchored on the campaign-defining URL pair: chatgpt.com/s/ (the lure surface, quoted verbatim from the article and code block) and openew[.]app (the off-platform download portal). The 30-min same-device join eliminates legitimate ChatGPT share-link usage that never leaves chatgpt.com. Corroborated by Malwarebytes write-up of the same domain serving Odyssey Stealer / Windows credential loader. Cross-checked against: • https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/threat-intel/2026/05/fake-chatgpt-download-site-infects-windows-and-mac-users-with-malware
ATT&CKT1583.008 T1566.002 T1204.001

[LLM] Browser download from openew[.]app or pinned LLMShare hosting IPs Delivery High
Detects a file-write event whose FileOriginUrl is openew[.]app — i.e. the moment the trojanised ChatGPT installer (Windows .exe or macOS .dmg) is dropped to disk by a browser. Pivots on the exact malware-hosting domain and its three resolved IPs from the article. Rationale: Pivots on the two installer SHA256s named in the article + openew[.]app as the FileOriginUrl, plus the three resolved IPs. The browser-process filter ensures we catch the moment the trojanised installer is saved to disk (the genuine TP) rather than every Chrome download. Cross-checked against: • https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/threat-intel/2026/05/fake-chatgpt-download-site-infects-windows-and-mac-users-with-malware

[LLM] Execution of LLMShare ChatGPT-installer SHA256 (Windows / macOS) Installation High
Process-creation alert keyed on the two installer hashes named in the article — c0919e19...(Windows) and c9e0e698...(macOS). Catches the moment the user double-clicks the trojanised ChatGPT installer, including cases where the file was sideloaded from USB/Teams/email rather than the browser path. Rationale: Article + linked VirusTotal pages name these two specific installer SHA256s. Process-hash match is the highest-fidelity IOC available and survives renaming/repackaging-of-container-but-not-binary. Cross-checked against: • https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/threat-intel/2026/05/fake-chatgpt-download-site-infects-windows-and-mac-users-with-malware

   or InitiatingProcessSHA256 in ("c9e0e6985dca3a179c9bdea4e7b38f7dc57fe00ecedc2fd634256fc53bf2de2d",
                                  "c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,

ImProcessCreate

          TargetProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] LLMShare anti-VM discovery: WMI BIOS/Computer queries + HKLM\HARDWARE reads post-installer launch Exploitation Medium
After the user runs the trojanised installer, the Windows payload enumerates VM/sandbox artefacts via WMI (Win32_ComputerSystem / Win32_BIOS) and reads HKLM\HARDWARE\DESCRIPTION\System before deciding to continue. Hunts that child-process / registry-read fan-out under a process whose parent matches the LLMShare installer hash or filename. Rationale: Anchored on the article's explicit anti-VM behaviour citation ("executes various commands to determine whether the device is a legitimate computer or a virtual machine") plus the kill-chain detection hint listing Win32_ComputerSystem / Win32_BIOS / HKLM\HARDWARE\DESCRIPTION\System. Parent-process scope is the LLMShare installer (hash or ChatGPT*.exe filename from Downloads/Temp) so generic admin VM-troubleshooting won't fire. Cross-checked against: • https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/threat-intel/2026/05/fake-chatgpt-download-site-infects-windows-and-mac-users-with-malware

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Registry
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let Window = 5m;
let InstallerLaunch = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where SHA256 == "c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b"
       or (FileName startswith "ChatGPT" and FolderPath has_any ("\\Downloads\\","\\Temp\\","\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\"))
    | project InstallTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName,
              InstallerPid = ProcessId, InstallerName = FileName,
              InstallerHash = SHA256;
let Children = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where FileName in~ ("wmic.exe","systeminfo.exe","tasklist.exe","reg.exe","cmd.exe","powershell.exe")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Win32_ComputerSystem","Win32_BIOS","Win32_BaseBoard",
                                         "computersystem","bios","hypervisor",
                                         "HARDWARE\\DESCRIPTION\\System",
                                         "Enum\\PCI","VBOX","VMware","VirtualBox")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessFileName,
              InitiatingProcessSHA256;
InstallerLaunch
| join kind=inner Children on DeviceId
| where Timestamp between (InstallTime .. InstallTime + Window)
| where InitiatingProcessId == InstallerPid or InitiatingProcessSHA256 == InstallerHash
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InstallerName, InstallerHash,
          DiscoveryBinary = FileName, DiscoveryCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, InstallTime)
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let Window = 5m;

    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where SHA256 == "c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b"
       or (TargetProcessName startswith "ChatGPT" and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Downloads","Temp"))
    | project InstallTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname,
              InstallerPid = TargetProcessId, InstallerName = TargetProcessName;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("wmic.exe","systeminfo.exe","tasklist.exe","reg.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Win32_ComputerSystem","Win32_BIOS","HARDWARE\\DESCRIPTION\\System","hypervisor","VBOX","VMware")

| where TimeGenerated between (InstallTime .. InstallTime + Window)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, InstallerName,
          DiscoveryBinary = TargetProcessName,
          DiscoveryCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', TimeGenerated, InstallTime)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process Exploitation High

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\winword.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\excel.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\powerpnt.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\outlook.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\onenote.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\mspub.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\visio.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |
    Word/Excel/Outlook/OneNote spawning powershell, cmd, wscript,
    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("188.137.246.189", "192.253.248.181", "172.94.9.250") or RemoteUrl has_any ("openew.app")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["188.137.246.189", "192.253.248.181", "172.94.9.250"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["openew.app"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("c9e0e6985dca3a179c9bdea4e7b38f7dc57fe00ecedc2fd634256fc53bf2de2d", "c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b") or SHA1 in~ ("c9e0e6985dca3a179c9bdea4e7b38f7dc57fe00ecedc2fd634256fc53bf2de2d", "c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b") or MD5 in~ ("c9e0e6985dca3a179c9bdea4e7b38f7dc57fe00ecedc2fd634256fc53bf2de2d", "c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("c9e0e6985dca3a179c9bdea4e7b38f7dc57fe00ecedc2fd634256fc53bf2de2d", "c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b") or SHA1 in~ ("c9e0e6985dca3a179c9bdea4e7b38f7dc57fe00ecedc2fd634256fc53bf2de2d", "c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b") or MD5 in~ ("c9e0e6985dca3a179c9bdea4e7b38f7dc57fe00ecedc2fd634256fc53bf2de2d", "c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["c9e0e6985dca3a179c9bdea4e7b38f7dc57fe00ecedc2fd634256fc53bf2de2d", "c0919e1999eaee67e67aeda0287722775afb04e9a9a0f727928b4d11265fb70b"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Claude Code ~/.claude.json MCP endpoint rewrite by non-Claude npm package Installation High
Hunts the ChatGPhish-adjacent vulnerability where a rogue npm package mutates the user-level Claude Code config (~/.claude.json) to substitute attacker-controlled MCP endpoints, MitM'ing OAuth-backed SaaS tokens. Triggers when node/npm/npx writes to the Claude Code global config but the invoking command line is NOT the official @anthropic-ai/claude-code package. Rationale: Article names the exact file (~/.claude.json) and the exact vector (rogue npm package rewriting MCP endpoints to interpose between Claude Code and an OAuth-backed MCP server). Web-search corroboration confirmed ~/.claude.json is the canonical Claude Code CLI global config (separate from project-local .mcp.json and Claude Desktop's claude_desktop_config.json), so writes to that exact path by an npm/node process whose command line is not the official package are high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp • https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/4976 • https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/develop/connect-local-servers
ATT&CKT1554 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ ".claude.json"
| where FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)\\Users\\[^\\]+\\\.claude\.json$"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","npx.exe","pnpm.exe","yarn.exe","bun.exe")
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("@anthropic-ai/claude-code","claude-code/cli","@anthropic-ai\\claude-code"))
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FolderPath, ActionType,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessParentId,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFileName =~ ".claude.json"
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)\\Users\\[^\\]+\\\.claude\.json$"
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\(node|npm|npx|pnpm|yarn|bun)\.exe$"
| where not(ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("@anthropic-ai/claude-code","claude-code/cli"))
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, EventType,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessId, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Claude Code Global Config Modified by Non-Claude NPM Process
id: a9f3c2e8-7b1d-4f5a-8c9e-2d3a4b5c6d7e
description: Detects writes to the Claude Code global MCP config (~/.claude.json) by node/npm/npx processes whose command line does not reference the official @anthropic-ai/claude-code package - matches the Permiso-documented rogue-npm-package MCP endpoint rewrite that MitMs OAuth-backed SaaS tokens.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/chatgphish-vulnerability-turns-chatgpt.html
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/29
tags:

logsource:

detection:

  selection_proc:

level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\\.claude.json OR *\\.CLAUDE.JSON OR *\\.Claude.json) @Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE OR *\\npm.exe OR *\\NPM.EXE OR *\\npx.exe OR *\\NPX.EXE OR *\\pnpm.exe OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\bun.exe) -@CommandLine:(*"@anthropic-ai/claude-code"* OR *"claude-code/cli"*)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\\\.claude\.json$/i ContextImageFileName=/\\(node|npm|npx|pnpm|yarn|bun)\.exe$/i
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 | NOT regex("(?i)@anthropic-ai/claude-code|claude-code/cli", field=CommandLine) | groupBy([aid, TargetProcessId], function=selectLast([CommandLine, ImageFileName]))}, field=[aid, ContextProcessId], key=[aid, TargetProcessId], include=[CommandLine, ImageFileName])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

[LLM] AI coding agent auto-spawns MCP server via npx -y from cloned workspace (TrustFall) Installation Medium
Hunts the Adversa-AI TrustFall pattern where a malicious repository ships a .mcp.json / claude_desktop_config.json with autoApprove enabled, causing Claude Code / Cursor / VS Code to launch an attacker MCP server (via `npx -y` or `uvx --from`) the moment the user clicks the 'Yes, I trust this folder' dialog - executing arbitrary code before any tool call. Rationale: Article specifies the TrustFall mechanic in detail: 'a configuration that auto-approves and spawns an MCP server', 'launching the attacker-controlled code with the developer's full system privileges', 'before any tool calls and without additional prompts'. The detectable byproduct is an AI-coding-agent process spawning node/npx/uvx with an auto-install flag and mcp in args - this is the actual execution channel even when the trigger config (.mcp.json) content isn't visible to EDR. Cross-checked against: • https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/develop/connect-local-servers • https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1218 T1195.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let AICodingAgents = dynamic(["claude.exe","cursor.exe","code.exe","windsurf.exe","cline.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (AICodingAgents)
| where FileName in~ ("node.exe","npx.cmd","npx.exe","uvx.exe","uv.exe","python.exe","deno.exe","bun.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("mcp","model-context-protocol","modelcontextprotocol","mcp-server","mcp_server")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(npx\s+(-y|--yes)|uvx\s+--from|pipx\s+run)"
| extend WorkspacePath = tostring(parse_path(InitiatingProcessCommandLine).Directory)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FileName,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          ChildPath = FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let AICodingAgents = dynamic(["claude.exe","cursor.exe","code.exe","windsurf.exe","cline.exe"]);
let RunnerBins = dynamic(["node.exe","npx.cmd","npx.exe","uvx.exe","uv.exe","python.exe","deno.exe","bun.exe"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName in~ (AICodingAgents)
| where ActingProcessName in~ (RunnerBins)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("mcp","model-context-protocol","modelcontextprotocol","mcp-server")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(npx\s+(-y|--yes)|uvx\s+--from|pipx\s+run)"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] OpenClaw skill HEARTBEAT.md modification - remote update prompt injection persistence Installation Medium
Hunts the OpenClaw skill remote-update vector where a benign-looking skill instructs the user to append attacker instructions to a HEARTBEAT.md file in the workspace - turning a static skill into an agent-influencing persistent prompt-injection surface. Flags creation or modification of HEARTBEAT.md anywhere in user-writable workspace paths. Rationale: Article names the exact filename - 'HEARTBEAT.md' - that the OpenClaw skill setup instructs the user to populate. Because this is a non-standard, agent-specific filename outside any common project convention, any HEARTBEAT.md write in a user workspace is worth hunting. Filtered out build artefact dirs to suppress accidental matches from packaged dependencies that happen to ship a similarly-named doc.
ATT&CKT1546 T1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "HEARTBEAT.md"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath !contains "\\node_modules\\"
      and FolderPath !contains "\\.git\\"
      and FolderPath !contains "\\build\\"
      and FolderPath !contains "\\dist\\"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), WriteCount = count(),
            Writers = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 10),
            SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
      by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FolderPath
| order by LastSeen desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName =~ "HEARTBEAT.md"
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFilePath !contains "\\node_modules\\"
      and TargetFilePath !contains "\\.git\\"
      and TargetFilePath !contains "\\build\\"
      and TargetFilePath !contains "\\dist\\"
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), WriteCount = count(),
            Writers = make_set(ActingProcessName, 10),
            SampleCmd = any(ActingProcessCommandLine)
      by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath
| order by LastSeen desc
title: OpenClaw Skill HEARTBEAT.md Created or Modified

[LLM] ChatGPhish - browser image fetch from chatgpt.com referer to non-OpenAI host (web proxy) Delivery Medium
Hunts the ChatGPhish primary attack surface where the chatgpt.com response renderer auto-fetches attacker-hosted images embedded in summarized web pages, leaking IP/UA/Referer and rendering clickable phishing links inside the trusted AI UI. Detects browser HTTP requests whose Referer is chatgpt.com but whose destination is not an OpenAI/Azure CDN, captured via web proxy / secure web gateway logs. Rationale: Article specifies the exact attack: chatgpt.com response renderer auto-fetches Markdown image URLs (leaking IP/UA/Referer) and renders Markdown links as clickable. The high-fidelity wire signal is HTTP Referer=chatgpt.com to a non-OpenAI image-hosting destination - perfectly expressible in web proxy / SWG logs and ASIM ImWebSession. Defender KQL is a weaker fallback that uses process-attributed network events + time-window correlation since EDR doesn't capture HTTP headers. Sigma is omitted because this is a multi-condition correlation rather than a single-event-shape match. CloudWatch is empty - no AWS angle.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1132.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let LookbackWindow = 7d;
let WindowSec = 30;
let Browsers = dynamic(["chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe","opera.exe"]);
let ChatGPT = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackWindow)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (Browsers)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any ("chatgpt.com","chat.openai.com")
    | project ChatTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, BrowserPid = InitiatingProcessId,
              Acct = InitiatingProcessAccountName;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackWindow)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (Browsers)
| where RemoteUrl matches regex @"(?i)(\.s3[\.-][a-z0-9-]+\.amazonaws\.com|\.r2\.dev|\.b-cdn\.net|blob\.core\.windows\.net|\.workers\.dev|firebasestorage\.googleapis\.com|\.pages\.dev|\.netlify\.app|\.vercel\.app|\.github\.io)"
| where not(RemoteUrl has_any ("openai.com","oaiusercontent.com","chatgpt.com","cdn.openai.com","oaistatic.com"))
| join kind=inner ChatGPT on DeviceId, $left.InitiatingProcessId == $right.BrowserPid
| where Timestamp between (ChatTime .. ChatTime + WindowSec * 1s)
| project ChatTime, FetchTime = Timestamp, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ChatTime),
          DeviceName, Acct, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ChatTime desc
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where HttpRequestHeaderReferer has_any ("chatgpt.com","chat.openai.com")
| where not(DstHostname endswith "openai.com"
         or DstHostname endswith "oaiusercontent.com"
         or DstHostname endswith "oaistatic.com"
         or DstHostname endswith "azureedge.net"
         or DstHostname endswith "gstatic.com")
| where DstHostname matches regex @"(?i)(\.s3[\.-][a-z0-9-]+\.amazonaws\.com|\.r2\.dev|\.b-cdn\.net|blob\.core\.windows\.net|\.workers\.dev|firebasestorage\.googleapis\.com|\.pages\.dev|\.netlify\.app|\.vercel\.app|\.github\.io)"
      or FileMimeType startswith "image/"
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstHostname, Url, HttpMethod, HttpRequestHeaderReferer, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, FileMimeType
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(zscaler.web OR netskope.alert OR bluecoat.proxysg OR cisco.umbrella) (@http.referrer:*chatgpt.com* OR @http.referer:*chatgpt.com*) -@http.url_details.host:(*.openai.com OR *.oaiusercontent.com OR *.oaistatic.com OR *.azureedge.net OR *.gstatic.com) (@http.url_details.host:(*.s3.amazonaws.com OR *.s3-*.amazonaws.com OR *.r2.dev OR *.b-cdn.net OR *.blob.core.windows.net OR *.workers.dev OR *.pages.dev OR *.netlify.app OR *.vercel.app OR *.github.io) OR @http.useragent:*image/*)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest ContextImageFileName=/\\(chrome|msedge|firefox|brave|arc|opera)\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)(\\.s3[\\.-][a-z0-9-]+\\.amazonaws\\.com|\\.r2\\.dev|\\.b-cdn\\.net|\\.blob\\.core\\.windows\\.net|\\.workers\\.dev|firebasestorage\\.googleapis\\.com|\\.pages\\.dev|\\.netlify\\.app|\\.vercel\\.app|\\.github\\.io)$", field=DomainName)
| join({#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(chatgpt\.com|chat\.openai\.com)$/i | groupBy([aid, ContextProcessId], function=min(@timestamp, as=chatgpt_time))}, field=[aid, ContextProcessId], include=[chatgpt_time])
| @timestamp >= chatgpt_time AND @timestamp <= chatgpt_time + 30000
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, DomainName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] vm2 vulnerable version inventory (CVE-2026-47140) — NodeVM denylist bypass surface Weaponization High
Surfaces hosts running npm:vm2 <= 3.11.3 which is vulnerable to the NodeVM builtin denylist bypass via the `process` and `inspector/promises` modules. Pre-incident asset hygiene UC to identify exposed Node.js services before exploitation. Rationale: Article names the affected package and version range (npm:vm2 <= 3.11.3) and the CVE ID directly. Cross-checked with The Hacker News reporting and Heise that the fix lands in vm2 3.11.4 alongside three sibling criticals (CVE-2026-47208/47137/47131). Internet-facing weighting added because vm2 is most dangerous when fronting an attacker-supplied JS-eval endpoint. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/vm2-nodejs-library-vulnerabilities.html • https://www.heise.de/en/news/Node-js-Four-critical-security-gaps-with-maximum-rating-in-vm2-closed-11300471.html • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rp36-8xq3-r6c4

[LLM] Node.js process spawning native shell / interpreter — post-vm2-escape host execution Exploitation Medium
Detects `node.exe` (or `node` on Linux) spawning a native shell or Windows LOLBin as a child process. After the CVE-2026-47140 escape, the attacker reaches `child_process.execFileSync(...)` in the host Node.js process — every successful exploitation surfaces here as an unexpected node→shell parent/child edge. Rationale: Article's PoC is `require("process").getBuiltinModule("child_process").execFileSync(...)` — every successful sandbox escape walks through node.exe → spawned-binary. Cross-checked with Hacker News and Semgrep coverage of the four sibling vm2 CVEs (47208/47137/47140/47131) confirming this parent/child edge is the common post-exploit primitive. The npm/yarn/pnpm filter strips the dominant FP class (lifecycle scripts). Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/vm2-nodejs-library-vulnerabilities.html • https://semgrep.dev/blog/2026/calling-back-to-vm2-and-escaping-sandbox/ • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rp36-8xq3-r6c4
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1059.003 T1059.001 T1190

[LLM] vm2 NodeVM denylist bypass PoC strings — getBuiltinModule + inspector/promises Exploitation High
Hunts for the literal sandbox-escape primitives from CVE-2026-47140: `getBuiltinModule("child_process")`, `require("inspector/promises")`, and `Runtime.evaluate` posted via an Inspector Session. These strings appearing in script content, written .js files, or process command lines is direct evidence of exploitation or PoC testing. Rationale: PoC strings from the advisory body are uniquely diagnostic — `getBuiltinModule("child_process")` and `require("inspector/promises")` are the literal escape primitives and have effectively zero benign use in production Node.js. Falcon's ScriptControlScanInfo (AMSI integration) carries the raw script body, making it the highest-fidelity surface; Defender/Sentinel fall back to process-cmdline + .js file writes outside node_modules. Cross-checked with Semgrep's coverage of the four sibling vm2 escapes confirming these are the new bypass tokens in the 3.11.4 patch. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/vm2-nodejs-library-vulnerabilities.html • https://semgrep.dev/blog/2026/calling-back-to-vm2-and-escaping-sandbox/ • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rp36-8xq3-r6c4

    | where FileName =~ "node.exe" or InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (bypass_tokens) or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (bypass_tokens)

let file_hits = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)

    | where FileName endswith ".js" or FileName endswith ".mjs" or FileName endswith ".cjs"

    | where FolderPath !contains @"\node_modules\"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source="FileEvents", Image=FolderPath, Cmd=tostring(strcat(FolderPath,"\\",FileName)), ParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256;
proc_hits
| union file_hits
| order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] Node.js process spawns shell or LOLBin — vm2 sandbox escape post-exploitation (CVE-2026-47210) Exploitation High
Hunts the universal vm2-escape pivot: a sandbox-escaped script reaches the host process and uses Node's child_process module to spawn cmd/powershell/sh/bash. The PoC for CVE-2026-47210 ends with `mainModule.require('child_process').execSync('touch pwned')` — any node.exe / node spawning a shell or scripting host is the high-fidelity signal because applications using vm2 as a security boundary should never have sandboxed code reach child_process. Rationale: Anchored on the exact post-escape sequence in the article's PoC: `e.constructor.constructor('return process')().mainModule.require('child_process').execSync(...)`. Once the JSPI bypass reaches host `process`, the attacker MUST cross from node into a child shell to do anything useful — there is no in-process payload step. Detection is article-grounded because vm2's whole purpose is preventing this; any node→shell parent-child is a sandbox failure. Cross-checked with Semgrep's vm2 escape write-up and TheHackerNews coverage which both confirm child_process as the universal pivot path. [LLM] Vulnerable vm2 (<= 3.11.3) present on host — CVE-2026-47210 exposure Reconnaissance Medium
Inventory hunt for hosts running Node.js applications that bundle a vulnerable vm2 version. Looks for vm2 package directory writes under node_modules and TVM coverage of CVE-2026-47210. Used to scope the blast radius and prioritise patching before any escape detection fires. Rationale: Article names the exact affected package and version range: `npm:vm2 (vuln <= 3.11.3)`. This UC pivots on that fact two ways — TVM lookup by CveId (CVE-2026-47210) for managed inventory, and file-path evidence of node_modules/vm2 for any host the TVM scanner missed (containers, dev workstations, CI runners). Confirmed package + CVE mapping via the GHSA advisory and SCW/SC Media coverage. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6j2x-vhqr-qr7q • https://www.scworld.com/brief/critical-vm2-vulnerability-allows-sandbox-escape-and-arbitrary-code-execution • https://www.isec.news/2026/05/07/vm2-library-hit-by-a-dozen-critical-node-js-sandbox-escape-flaws/
ATT&CKT1592.002

    | where CveId == "CVE-2026-47210"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel;
let VulnByFile = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FolderPath has @"\node_modules\vm2\" or FolderPath has "/node_modules/vm2/"
    | where FileName =~ "package.json"
    | summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), Paths = make_set(FolderPath, 10) by DeviceId, DeviceName
    | project Timestamp = LastSeen, DeviceId, DeviceName, Evidence = "node_modules/vm2 package.json present", Paths;
VulnByTvm
| union VulnByFile
| order by Timestamp desc
let VulnByTvm = DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

    | project TimeGenerated, DeviceId, DeviceName, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel;
let VulnByFile = ImFileEvent

    | project TimeGenerated = LastSeen, DvcHostname, Evidence = "node_modules/vm2 package.json present", Paths;
VulnByTvm

| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Node.js process spawning OS shell with enumeration commands — vm2 sandbox escape (CVE-2026-47137) Exploitation Medium
Hunts for node/node.exe directly spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, sh, or bash to execute reconnaissance commands (id, whoami, uname, /etc/passwd reads). This is the post-exploitation signature of a vm2 NodeVM sandbox escape via the nesting:true patch bypass, where attacker JS inside the sandbox reaches child_process.execSync on the host. The PoC in the advisory literally runs `id` via execSync. Rationale: Anchored on the advisory's PoC which spawns `child_process.execSync('id')` from inside the nested NodeVM. Node spawning a system shell is unusual outside of build tooling/CI; pairing the parent=node predicate with classic recon command-line tokens (whoami, id, uname, /etc/passwd) gives a high-fidelity post-exploit signal. CVE-2023-37903 (referenced in advisory) is the original sandbox escape this bypass revives. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8hg8-63c5-gwmx
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.003 T1059.004 T1611

| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe", "node")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "sh", "bash", "dash", "ash", "zsh", "wmic.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("whoami", " id ", " id;", "uname", "hostname", "ipconfig", "ifconfig", "/etc/passwd", "/etc/shadow", "child_process", "execSync", "net user", "cat /etc", "systeminfo")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\node.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "/node" or ParentProcessName =~ "node.exe" or ParentProcessName =~ "node"
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "/sh", "/bash", "/dash", "/zsh", "wmic.exe")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("whoami", " id ", "uname", "hostname", "ipconfig", "ifconfig", "/etc/passwd", "/etc/shadow", "child_process", "execSync", "net user", "cat /etc", "systeminfo")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine

[LLM] Vulnerable vm2 package (<=3.11.3) present on host — CVE-2026-47137 exposure surface Weaponization High
Hunts for vm2 npm package installs on endpoints/servers — the package's package.json under any node_modules\vm2 path. vm2 was deprecated and ANY version <=3.11.3 is vulnerable to the nesting:true patch bypass that produces full RCE. Use this to inventory exposure for the CVE-2026-47137 mitigation campaign. Rationale: The advisory explicitly names the vulnerable package (npm:vm2 <=3.11.3) and the patched-but-bypassed file (nodevm.js line 263). File-presence telemetry for node_modules/vm2/package.json gives a complete exposure inventory; nodevm.js presence is a precision pivot to the exact vulnerable code path. Triage on file content/version is a follow-up step the SOC runs after the hunt surfaces hosts. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8hg8-63c5-gwmx
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007

DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(90d)
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\node_modules\vm2\", "/node_modules/vm2/")
| where FileName in~ ("package.json", "nodevm.js", "main.js", "index.js")
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen  = max(Timestamp),
            Paths     = make_set(FolderPath, 20),
            Files     = make_set(FileName, 10),
            Writers   = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 10)
  by DeviceName
| extend NodeAppHost = iff(array_length(Paths) > 0, true, false)
| order by LastSeen desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("\\node_modules\\vm2\\", "/node_modules/vm2/")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("package.json", "nodevm.js", "main.js", "index.js")
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen  = max(TimeGenerated),
            Paths     = make_set(TargetFilePath, 20),
            Files     = make_set(TargetFileName, 10),
            Writers   = make_set(ActingProcessName, 10)
  by DvcHostname
| order by LastSeen desc
title: vm2 npm Package Present on Host - CVE-2026-47137 Exposure
id: 4d2e7c91-3b5f-4a82-b7c1-9e6f8d0a2c14
description: Detects file-system presence of the vm2 npm package (package.json under node_modules/vm2). All versions <=3.11.3 are vulnerable to the nesting:true patch bypass disclosed in CVE-2026-47137 (bypass of CVE-2023-37903), enabling full RCE from inside the sandbox.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-m4wx-m65x-ghrr
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1190
logsource:
  category: file_event
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\node_modules\vm2\'
      - '/node_modules/vm2/'
  selection_file:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '\package.json'
      - '/package.json'
      - '\nodevm.js'
      - '/nodevm.js'
  condition: selection and selection_file
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate applications that bundle vm2 — confirm version and apply mitigations
  - Developer workstations with cloned repos containing vm2 in dependencies
level: medium
source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd) @EventID:(11 OR 1) (@TargetFilename:(*\\node_modules\\vm2\\package.json OR *\\node_modules\\vm2\\lib\\nodevm.js OR */node_modules/vm2/package.json OR */node_modules/vm2/lib/nodevm.js) OR @file.path:(*/node_modules/vm2/package.json OR */node_modules/vm2/lib/nodevm.js))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| regex("(\\\\|\\/)node_modules(\\\\|\\/)vm2(\\\\|\\/)(package\\.json|lib(\\\\|\\/)nodevm\\.js|main\\.js|index\\.js)$", field=TargetFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
| sort(field=ComputerName)
ENDPOINT

[LLM] Vulnerable vm2 package (<=3.11.3) present on endpoints — CVE-2026-47208 exposure Weaponization High
Hunts file-system evidence of the vm2 npm package at vulnerable versions deployed on hosts. The PoC requires the vm2 module to be loaded; any node_modules/vm2/package.json on disk with version <= 3.11.3 is a direct exposure indicator. Use this to bound the vulnerable surface before behavioral hunts. Rationale: Article explicitly names affected package as 'npm:vm2 (vuln <= 3.11.3)'. Detecting node_modules/vm2/package.json on disk is the cleanest exposure indicator before behavioral exploitation. Corroborated against vm2 GitHub advisory and TheHackerNews 2026 vm2 wave write-up. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/patriksimek/vm2/security/advisories/GHSA-qvjj-29qf-hp7p • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/vm2-nodejs-library-vulnerabilities.html • https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/vm2/CVE-2026-24120/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
// Hunts vm2 package.json drops on disk; pair with DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory if Node modules ingested

| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "package.json"
| where FolderPath has @"\node_modules\vm2\" or FolderPath has "/node_modules/vm2/"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// ASIM file-event variant — covers vendors shipping file telemetry to Sentinel
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName =~ "package.json"
| where TargetFilePath has @"\node_modules\vm2\" or TargetFilePath has "/node_modules/vm2/"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] node.exe spawning child_process targets — vm2 Promise species sandbox escape post-exploitation Exploitation Medium
Detects the post-escape pattern from CVE-2026-47208 PoC where the attacker uses ex.constructor.constructor('return process')().mainModule.require('child_process').execSync(...) to spawn arbitrary host processes from inside a vm2 sandbox. Filters for node.exe parent spawning shells/cmd/touch/curl/wget without a benign build-tool ancestor. Rationale: PoC ends in 'ex.constructor.constructor("return process")().mainModule.require(\'child_process\').execSync(\'touch pwned\')'. The detectable observable is node.exe parent spawning child_process targets without a benign npm/yarn/electron build-tool ancestor. Corroborated against TheHackerNews 2026 vm2 wave coverage and Kodem analysis of AI-agent RCE risk. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/patriksimek/vm2/security/advisories/GHSA-qvjj-29qf-hp7p • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/vm2-nodejs-library-vulnerabilities.html • https://www.kodemsecurity.com/resources/vm2-sandbox-escape-vulnerabilities-the-2026-cve-wave-turning-ai-agents-into-host-rce-vectors
ATT&CKT1068 T1059.007 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
// vm2 sandbox escape -> child_process.execSync spawns host process from node.exe
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","touch.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","npm ci","npm run","yarn install","pnpm install","node-gyp","electron-builder","husky","postinstall"))
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd  = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildPath  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd   = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256, ProcessIntegrityLevel
| order by Timestamp desc
// ASIM process-create — node.exe parent spawning shell/cmd/touch after vm2 escape
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName endswith "node.exe"
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","touch.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","certutil.exe")
| where not (ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","npm ci","npm run","yarn","pnpm","node-gyp","electron","postinstall","husky"))
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

  child:
    Image|endswith:

      - '\powershell.exe'

[LLM] vm2 Promise species sandbox escape PoC fingerprint in scripts/command lines Weaponization High
Hunts the specific JavaScript exploitation idiom from CVE-2026-47208 PoC: combinations of Symbol.species class extension of Promise, ex.constructor.constructor('return process')(), and mainModule.require('child_process'). These strings appear in attacker payloads delivered to vm2-using services and in saved exploit files. Rationale: The PoC contains highly distinctive idioms: 'ex.constructor.constructor("return process")()' for breaking out via the prototype chain, 'mainModule.require(\'child_process\')' for arbitrary execution, and 'Symbol.species' class extension of Promise — the actual vulnerable mechanism. These three strings together are extremely rare in benign code. Sigma omitted because the detection chains union/joins across cmdline and file telemetry — single-event shape doesn't fit. Corroborated against the GitHub advisory PoC and GitLab CVE-2026-24120 advisory of the same Promise.species root cause. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-76w7-j9cq-rx2j • https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/vm2/CVE-2026-24120/ • https://github.com/patriksimek/vm2/security/advisories/GHSA-qvjj-29qf-hp7p
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
// Hunts CVE-2026-47208 PoC fingerprint in node.exe cmdlines AND .js file drops
let poc_strings = dynamic([
    "constructor.constructor(\"return process\")",
    "constructor.constructor('return process')",
    "mainModule.require('child_process')",
    "mainModule.require(\"child_process\")",
    "Symbol.species"
]);
let cmdline_hits =
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName in~ ("node.exe","nodejs.exe")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (poc_strings)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Source = "cmdline",
              Evidence = ProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
let file_hits =
    DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName endswith ".js" or FileName endswith ".mjs" or FileName endswith ".cjs"
    | where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (poc_strings) or FolderPath has "vm2"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              Source = "file",
              Evidence = strcat(FolderPath, "\\", FileName),
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
union cmdline_hits, file_hits
| order by Timestamp desc
// Sentinel ImProcessCreate variant — PoC strings in node.exe command lines
let poc_strings = dynamic([
    'constructor.constructor("return process")',
    "constructor.constructor('return process')",
    "mainModule.require('child_process')",
    'mainModule.require("child_process")',
    "Symbol.species"
]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("node.exe","nodejs.exe")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (poc_strings)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:*\\node.exe OR @Image:*\\Node.exe OR @Image:*\\NODE.EXE) (@CommandLine:*constructor.constructor* OR @CommandLine:*mainModule.require* OR @CommandLine:*Symbol.species*Promise*)
(#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 OR #event_simpleName=ScriptControlScanInfo)
| (regex("constructor\\.constructor\\([\"']return process[\"']\\)", field=CommandLine) OR regex("mainModule\\.require\\([\"']child_process[\"']\\)", field=CommandLine) OR regex("Symbol\\.species", field=ScriptContent) OR regex("constructor\\.constructor\\([\"']return process[\"']\\)", field=ScriptContent))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, HostName, CommandLine], function=count())
