Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender

Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] HLS Installer.874.exe DLL side-load drops malicious library (Securelist fake-plugin miner) · [LLM] Fake GoogleUpdateTaskMachineQC scheduled-task/service persistence (SilentCryptoMiner derivative) · [LLM] Defender exclusion added for C:\ProgramData\Google\Chrome (miner staging dir) · [LLM] explorer.exe writes EXE/DLL into C:\ProgramData\Google\Chrome (miner watchdog restore) · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] C2 callback to Securelist fake-plugin miner .space rotating domains / config IP 107.172.212.235 · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains · DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] HLS Installer.874.exe DLL side-load drops malicious library (Securelist fake-plugin miner) Installation High
Hunts the article's exact delivery primitive: the legitimate-looking 'HLS Installer.874.exe' from a ZIP archive loading the side-loaded malicious DLL (SHA1 6a0fe60...) that decrypts the SilentCryptoMiner/RAT chain. Pivots on the installer image name combined with image-load events of the known-bad hash or a non-system path. Rationale: Pivots on the article's exact named installer 'HLS Installer.874.exe' plus the published SHA1/SHA256 of the side-loaded malicious DLL. Both image-load and process-create paths covered because side-load can manifest as either a process or an image load. Cross-checked with Securelist's writeup (https://securelist.com/video-books-pirates-miners-rat/119943/) which confirms the installer name and DLL pairing. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/video-books-pirates-miners-rat/119943/
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let badSha1 = "6a0fe6065d76715feebc1526d456db737f624407";
let installer = "HLS Installer.874.exe";
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ installer or InitiatingProcessFileName =~ installer or ProcessCommandLine has "HLS Installer.874.exe" or SHA1 == badSha1
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| union (
    DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ installer
    | where SHA1 == badSha1 or (FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\" and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
  )
| order by Timestamp desc
let badSha1 = "6a0fe6065d76715feebc1526d456db737f624407";
union isfuzzy=true
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where NewProcessName endswith @"\HLS Installer.874.exe" or CommandLine has "HLS Installer.874.exe"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, SubjectUserName),
(ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where TargetProcessName has "HLS Installer.874.exe" or SHA1 =~ badSha1
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ActorUsername, SHA1),
(ImFileEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where TargetFileSHA1 =~ badSha1 or TargetFileName =~ "HLS Installer.874.exe"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA1)
title: HLS Installer.874.exe Execution (Securelist Fake Video Plugin Miner)
id: a3c5fbd2-1b2a-4d70-8b59-9c2c46f1d2a1
status: experimental
description: Detects execution of the staging binary 'HLS Installer.874.exe' or its known-bad SHA1 side-loaded DLL used by the SilentCryptoMiner-derived campaign distributed via fake video-player plugin updates on pirate streaming sites.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/video-books-pirates-miners-rat/119943/
  - https://cybersecuritynews.com/hackers-use-fake-video-player-updates/

#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2

[LLM] Fake GoogleUpdateTaskMachineQC scheduled-task/service persistence (SilentCryptoMiner derivative) Installation High
Detects creation of the article's specific persistence artefact — a scheduled task or service masquerading as 'GoogleUpdateTaskMachineQC' that re-launches the miner on every boot. The real Google Updater task name is 'GoogleUpdateTaskMachineCore' / '...UA' — the 'QC' suffix is the attacker's tell. Rationale: The article explicitly names the persistence artefact 'GoogleUpdateTaskMachineQC' — the legitimate Google Updater uses '...Core' and '...UA' suffixes, so 'QC' is a deterministic IOC. Covers all three creation vectors (schtasks/sc/reg) plus the resulting registry footprint. Securelist (https://securelist.com/video-books-pirates-miners-rat/119943/) confirms this exact name and that it is registered as both task and service. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/video-books-pirates-miners-rat/119943/
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1543.003 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Registry
let task = "GoogleUpdateTaskMachineQC";
union isfuzzy=true
(DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ProcessCommandLine has task
  | where FileName in~ ("schtasks.exe","sc.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","reg.exe","cmd.exe","wmic.exe")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath),
(DeviceRegistryEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where (RegistryKey has @"\Services\GoogleUpdateTaskMachineQC")
       or (RegistryKey has @"\Schedule\TaskCache\Tasks\" and RegistryValueData has task)
       or RegistryValueName =~ "GoogleUpdateTaskMachineQC"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| order by Timestamp desc
let task = "GoogleUpdateTaskMachineQC";
union isfuzzy=true
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where EventID in (4698, 4697, 4688)
  | where CommandLine has task or EventData has task or ServiceName =~ task or ServiceFileName has task
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, EventID, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ServiceName, ServiceFileName, SubjectUserName),
(Event
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Source =~ "Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler"
  | where EventData has task
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, EventID, RenderedDescription),
(ImRegistryEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where RegistryKey has @"\Services\GoogleUpdateTaskMachineQC" or RegistryValueData has task
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName)

  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\schtasks.exe'
      - '\sc.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\reg.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\wmic.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'GoogleUpdateTaskMachineQC'

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate Google Updater uses GoogleUpdateTaskMachineCore / GoogleUpdateTaskMachineUA — NOT the QC suffix
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) (@EventID:(1 OR 4688 OR 4698 OR 4697) OR @EventID:13) (@CommandLine:*GoogleUpdateTaskMachineQC* OR @ServiceName:*GoogleUpdateTaskMachineQC* OR @TargetObject:(*\Services\GoogleUpdateTaskMachineQC* OR *\TaskCache\Tasks\*GoogleUpdateTaskMachineQC*) OR @ServiceFileName:*GoogleUpdateTaskMachineQC*)
(#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 (CommandLine=/GoogleUpdateTaskMachineQC/i) (ImageFileName=/(schtasks|sc|powershell|pwsh|reg|cmd|wmic)\.exe$/i)) OR (#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate (RegObjectName=/\\Services\\GoogleUpdateTaskMachineQC/i OR RegStringValue=/GoogleUpdateTaskMachineQC/i OR RegValueName=/GoogleUpdateTaskMachineQC/i))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, RegObjectName, RegStringValue], function=count())

[LLM] C2 callback to Securelist fake-plugin miner .space rotating domains / config IP 107.172.212.235 Command & Control High
Sweeps endpoint network telemetry for connections or DNS queries to the article's rotating RAT C2 .space domains (5d14vnfb, r7mvjl67, zgj1tam9, jeaw520i, qdmagva5), the staging domain urush1bar4.online, the UnamWebPanel control panel domains (m4yuri.online, kristina.quest), and the SilentCryptoMiner config-retrieval IP 107.172.212.235. Rationale: Built on the IOC table verbatim: 5 rotating RAT C2 .space domains (one per quarter since April 2025), the urush1bar4.online staging URL, the two UnamWebPanel control-panel domains (m4yuri.online + kristina.quest), and the miner-config-retrieval IP 107.172.212.235. Cross-checked against Securelist (https://securelist.com/video-books-pirates-miners-rat/119943/) which describes the same campaign and IOC set. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/video-books-pirates-miners-rat/119943/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004 T1568.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
let badDomains = dynamic(["5d14vnfb.space","r7mvjl67.space","zgj1tam9.space","jeaw520i.space","qdmagva5.space","urush1bar4.online","m4yuri.online","kristina.quest"]);
let badIPs = dynamic(["107.172.212.235"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (badIPs)
   or RemoteUrl has_any (badDomains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let badDomains = dynamic(["5d14vnfb.space","r7mvjl67.space","zgj1tam9.space","jeaw520i.space","qdmagva5.space","urush1bar4.online","m4yuri.online","kristina.quest"]);
let badIPs = dynamic(["107.172.212.235"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Name has_any (badDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, IPAddresses=Result),
(ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any (badDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DnsQuery, DnsResponseCodeName),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DestinationIP in (badIPs) or RequestURL has_any (badDomains) or DestinationHostName has_any (badDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, DeviceProduct),
(ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DstIpAddr in (badIPs) or DstHostname has_any (badDomains) or Url has_any (badDomains)
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, Url)

[LLM] Defender exclusion added for C:\ProgramData\Google\Chrome (miner staging dir) Installation High
Catches the article's defense-evasion step: the miner adds Windows Defender exclusions for EXE/DLL files and the C:\ProgramData\Google\Chrome folder it lives in, so the watchdog and miner survive AV scans. Covers both the PowerShell Add-MpPreference path and direct Defender exclusion registry writes. Rationale: Article and Securelist both explicitly state the miner adds Defender exclusions for EXE/DLL extensions AND for system folders that resolve to its staging dir C:\ProgramData\Google\Chrome. Detection ties the Add-MpPreference verb to that specific path (or the wider 'ExclusionExtension .exe/.dll' pattern that's atypical of legitimate sysadmin work). Cross-checked against https://securelist.com/video-books-pirates-miners-rat/119943/. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/video-books-pirates-miners-rat/119943/
ATT&CKT1562.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Registry
union isfuzzy=true
(DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe")
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Add-MpPreference","Set-MpPreference")
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (@"ProgramData\Google\Chrome", "ExclusionPath", "ExclusionExtension", ".exe", ".dll")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath),
(DeviceRegistryEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where RegistryKey has @"Windows Defender\Exclusions"
  | where RegistryValueName has_any (@"C:\ProgramData\Google\Chrome", ".exe", ".dll")
     or RegistryValueData has @"C:\ProgramData\Google\Chrome"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where NewProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe")
  | where CommandLine has_any ("Add-MpPreference","Set-MpPreference")
  | where CommandLine has_any (@"ProgramData\Google\Chrome","ExclusionPath","ExclusionExtension")
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, SubjectUserName),
(ImRegistryEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where RegistryKey has @"Windows Defender\Exclusions"
  | where RegistryValue has_any (@"C:\ProgramData\Google\Chrome",".exe",".dll") or RegistryValueData has @"C:\ProgramData\Google\Chrome"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName)
title: Defender Exclusion for C:\ProgramData\Google\Chrome (Fake Plugin Miner)
id: 7e6f5d4c-3b2a-1098-7654-321fedcba098
status: experimental
description: Detects the SilentCryptoMiner-derivative behaviour of registering Add-MpPreference / registry exclusions targeting C:\ProgramData\Google\Chrome plus EXE/DLL extensions, as described in the Securelist fake-video-plugin campaign.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/video-books-pirates-miners-rat/119943/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.t1562.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'Add-MpPreference'
      - 'Set-MpPreference'
  selection_target:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'ProgramData\Google\Chrome'
      - 'ExclusionPath'
      - 'ExclusionExtension'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_target
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) ((@EventID:(1 OR 4688) @Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\cmd.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe) @CommandLine:(*Add-MpPreference* OR *Set-MpPreference*) @CommandLine:(*ProgramData\Google\Chrome* OR *ExclusionPath* OR *ExclusionExtension*)) OR (@EventID:13 @TargetObject:(*Windows\ Defender\Exclusions* OR *windows\ defender\exclusions*)))
(#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|cmd)\.exe$/i CommandLine=/(Add|Set)-MpPreference/i CommandLine=/(ProgramData\\Google\\Chrome|ExclusionPath|ExclusionExtension)/i) OR (#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate RegObjectName=/Windows Defender\\Exclusions/i (RegValueName=/ProgramData\\Google\\Chrome|\.exe$|\.dll$/i OR RegStringValue=/ProgramData\\Google\\Chrome/i))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, RegObjectName, RegValueName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe") AND (Processes.process="*Add-MpPreference*" OR Processes.process="*Set-MpPreference*") AND (Processes.process="*ProgramData\\Google\\Chrome*" OR Processes.process="*ExclusionPath*" OR Processes.process="*ExclusionExtension*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe") AND (Processes.process="*Add-MpPreference*" OR Processes.process="*Set-MpPreference*") AND (Processes.process="*ProgramData\\Google\\Chrome*" OR Processes.process="*ExclusionPath*" OR Processes.process="*ExclusionExtension*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
[LLM] explorer.exe writes EXE/DLL into C:\ProgramData\Google\Chrome (miner watchdog restore) Installation High
Detects the watchdog component the article describes: code running inside explorer.exe checks every 5 seconds that the miner exists in C:\ProgramData\Google\Chrome and restores it from an encrypted backup if removed. explorer.exe writing PE files to that directory is highly anomalous and is the watchdog's restoration write. Rationale: Article explicitly: 'A watchdog component running inside Windows Explorer checks every five seconds to confirm the miner is active, restoring it from an encrypted backup if anything is removed.' Combines that behaviour with the staging path C:\ProgramData\Google\Chrome that Securelist confirms. explorer.exe writing PE files anywhere is rare; into a 'Google' subdirectory of ProgramData specifically is essentially zero-FP. Cross-checked against https://securelist.com/video-books-pirates-miners-rat/119943/. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/video-books-pirates-miners-rat/119943/
ATT&CKT1055.012 T1546 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "explorer.exe"
| where FolderPath startswith @"C:\ProgramData\Google\Chrome"
| where FileName endswith ".exe" or FileName endswith ".dll" or FileName endswith ".bin" or FileName endswith ".dat"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA1, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has "explorer.exe"
| where TargetFilePath startswith @"C:\ProgramData\Google\Chrome"
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("exe","dll","bin","dat")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA1, TargetFileSHA256, EventType
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: explorer.exe Writes PE to C:\ProgramData\Google\Chrome (Fake Plugin Miner Watchdog)
id: 9a8b7c6d-5e4f-3210-fedc-ba9876543210
status: experimental
description: explorer.exe is the watchdog host for the SilentCryptoMiner-derivative described by Securelist. Every 5 seconds it confirms the miner binary in C:\ProgramData\Google\Chrome and restores it from an encrypted backup if missing. Legitimate explorer.exe should never drop PE files into that path.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/video-books-pirates-miners-rat/119943/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.t1055.012
  - attack.t1546
  - attack.t1036.005
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\explorer.exe'
    TargetFilename|startswith: 'C:\ProgramData\Google\Chrome'
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '.exe'
      - '.dll'
      - '.bin'
      - '.dat'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\explorer.exe OR *\Explorer.exe OR *\EXPLORER.EXE) @TargetFilename:(*\ProgramData\Google\Chrome\* OR *\programdata\google\chrome\*) @TargetFilename:(*.exe OR *.dll OR *.bin OR *.dat)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| ContextImageFileName=/\\explorer\.exe$/i
| TargetFileName=/\\ProgramData\\Google\\Chrome\\/i
| TargetFileName=/\.(exe|dll|bin|dat)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_name) as files values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name="explorer.exe" AND Filesystem.file_path="*ProgramData\\Google\\Chrome*" AND (Filesystem.file_name="*.exe" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.dll") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries Command & Control Medium
Long subdomain labels + frequent queries to a single 2LD = DNS C2/exfil.
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1048.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort == 53 and isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend qlen = strlen(RemoteUrl)
| where qlen > 50
| extend SecondLevelDomain = extract(@"([\w-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,})$", 1, RemoteUrl)
| summarize qcount = count(), uniqueSubs = dcount(RemoteUrl), maxLabel = max(qlen)
    by DeviceName, SecondLevelDomain
| where qcount > 100 and uniqueSubs > 20
| order by qcount desc
// ASIM ImDnsActivity normalises Windows DNS, Sysmon EID 22, Linux dnsmasq, etc.
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where DnsQueryTypeName == "TXT"
| summarize Queries = count(), DistinctNames = dcount(DnsQuery)
            by SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where Queries > 200    // tune to TXT-query baseline for environment
| order by Queries desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6A0FE6065D76715FEEBC1526D456DB737F624407") or SHA1 in~ ("6A0FE6065D76715FEEBC1526D456DB737F624407") or MD5 in~ ("6A0FE6065D76715FEEBC1526D456DB737F624407")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6A0FE6065D76715FEEBC1526D456DB737F624407") or SHA1 in~ ("6A0FE6065D76715FEEBC1526D456DB737F624407") or MD5 in~ ("6A0FE6065D76715FEEBC1526D456DB737F624407")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["6A0FE6065D76715FEEBC1526D456DB737F624407"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0b
status: experimental

2026-05-29 20 use cases 10 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

GREYVIBE, per WithSecure, is assessed to be a Russian-speaking group operating broadly in the Russian time zone, with the activities aligning with Kremlin state interests, specifically when it comes to

[LLM] GREYVIBE ClickFix fake Zoom/LAPAS CAPTCHA paste into Win+R then PowerShell Delivery High
Hunts the ClickFix initial-access pattern where a user lands on a fake Zoom/LAPAS CAPTCHA page (zoomconference.click/.app, lapas.live) and is coached to paste an attacker-supplied command into the Run dialog, spawning powershell.exe or mshta.exe from explorer.exe. This is GREYVIBE's documented entry path for the PhantomRelay/LegionRelay infection chain. Rationale: Article explicitly names zoomconference.click/.app and lapas.live as the ClickFix CAPTCHA domains, and the kill-chain phase-2 detection hint calls out explorer→powershell/mshta with Win+R paste indicators. The parent=explorer + suspicious cradle string + 5-minute proximity to a lure-domain visit on the same device is high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/002/ • https://www.proofpoint.com/us/blog/threat-insight/clickfix-malware-campaign-attack
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "explorer.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("iex ","Invoke-Expression","DownloadString","FromBase64String","-EncodedCommand","-enc ","-W Hidden","-WindowStyle Hidden","curl ","Invoke-RestMethod")
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceNetworkEvents | where Timestamp > ago(7d) | where RemoteUrl has_any ("zoomconference.click","zoomconference.app","lapas.live") | project DeviceId, ClickTime=Timestamp, BadUrl=RemoteUrl) on DeviceId
| where isnull(ClickTime) or Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 5m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ParentImage=InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ChildImage=FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, BadUrl, ClickTime
| order by Timestamp desc
let LureDomains = dynamic(["zoomconference.click","zoomconference.app","lapas.live","strip-mens.tilda.ws"]);
let Visits = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where Url has_any (LureDomains)
    | project ClickTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, Url;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\explorer.exe"
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\mshta.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\cscript.exe")
| where CommandLine has_any ("iex ","Invoke-Expression","DownloadString","FromBase64String","-EncodedCommand","-enc ","-W Hidden","-WindowStyle Hidden","curl ","Invoke-RestMethod")
| join kind=leftouter Visits on $left.Computer == $right.DvcHostname
| where isnull(ClickTime) or TimeGenerated between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 5m)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, Url, ClickTime
title: GREYVIBE ClickFix Win+R Paste Spawns PowerShell or mshta
id: 1a3c8b2e-9d6f-4a51-bb3c-7e2c4f5a1b22
description: Detects explorer.exe spawning powershell.exe/mshta.exe with download or encoded-command cradles consistent with the GREYVIBE ClickFix CAPTCHA paste lure (zoomconference.click/.app, lapas.live).
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/new-russian-linked-greyvibe-targets.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.t1566.002
  - attack.t1204.001
  - attack.t1059.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\explorer.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'iex '
      - 'Invoke-Expression'
      - 'DownloadString'
      - 'FromBase64String'
      - '-EncodedCommand'
      - '-enc '
      - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
      - 'Invoke-RestMethod'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\explorer.exe OR *\\Explorer.EXE) @Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\mshta.exe OR *\\MSHTA.EXE OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\WScript.exe) @CommandLine:(*iex* OR *Invoke-Expression* OR *DownloadString* OR *FromBase64String* OR *EncodedCommand* OR *Invoke-RestMethod*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/explorer\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|mshta|wscript|cscript)\.exe$/i
| regex("(iex |Invoke-Expression|DownloadString|FromBase64String|-EncodedCommand|-enc |WindowStyle Hidden|Invoke-RestMethod)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="explorer.exe" Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe") (Processes.process="*RunMRU*" OR Processes.process="*iex *" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*" OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-W Hidden*" OR Processes.process="*-EncodedCommand*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="explorer.exe" Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe") (Processes.process="*RunMRU*" OR Processes.process="*iex *" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*" OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-W Hidden*" OR Processes.process="*-EncodedCommand*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
[LLM] GREYVIBE PhantomMail Google Drive / 4sync archive lure delivered via email Delivery Medium
Detects inbound email containing links to Google Drive or 4sync that resolve to ZIP/RAR archives, which is GREYVIBE's PhantomMail spear-phishing delivery for JavaScript-based loaders that drop a decoy document and launch PhantomRelay. Correlates the email URL with subsequent archive extraction and JS execution on the recipient host. Rationale: Article specifies that PhantomMail emails carried links to Google Drive and 4sync archives containing JavaScript loaders, and the kill chain identifies wscript/cscript from extracted archive paths as the execution pivot. Correlating the email-side IOC (cloud-archive URLs) with the host-side JS-loader execution within a 6h window cuts FPs from legitimate file-share usage. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/002/
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes
let SuspiciousUrls = EmailUrlInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where Url has_any ("drive.google.com","4sync.com","4shared.com")
    | where Url has_any (".zip",".rar","download","uc?id=","file/d/");
let Recipients = EmailEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where DeliveryAction in ("Delivered","DeliveredAsSpam")
    | join kind=inner SuspiciousUrls on NetworkMessageId
    | project EmailTime=Timestamp, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress, Subject, Url, NetworkMessageId;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (".js",".jse",".vbs",".wsf")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\Downloads\",@"\Temp\",@"\AppData\Local\Temp\",@"\7-Zip\",@"\WinRAR\")
| join kind=inner (Recipients) on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| where Timestamp between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 6h)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountUpn, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Url, Subject, SenderFromAddress
let SuspectUrls = dynamic(["drive.google.com","4sync.com","4shared.com"]);
let Recips = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where Operation in ("MailItemsAccessed","Send")
    | extend Url = tostring(parse_json(Parameters))
    | where Url has_any (SuspectUrls) and Url has_any (".zip",".rar","file/d/","uc?id=")
    | project EmailTime=TimeGenerated, RecipientEmailAddress=UserId, Url;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\wscript.exe","\\cscript.exe")
| where CommandLine has_any (".js",".jse",".vbs",".wsf")
| where CommandLine has_any ("\\Downloads\\","\\Temp\\","\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\")
| join kind=inner Recips on $left.TargetUserName == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 6h)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, TargetUserName, CommandLine, NewProcessName, ParentProcessName, Url
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\wscript.exe OR *\\WScript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\CScript.exe) @CommandLine:(*.js* OR *.jse* OR *.vbs* OR *.wsf*) @CommandLine:(*\\Downloads\\* OR *\\Temp\\* OR *\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(wscript|cscript)\.exe$/i
| regex("\\.(js|jse|vbs|wsf)", field=CommandLine)
| regex("\\\\(Downloads|Temp|AppData\\\\Local\\\\Temp)\\\\", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())

| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Email.All_Email where (All_Email.url="*drive.google.com/*" OR All_Email.url="*4sync.com/*" OR All_Email.url="*4shared.com/*") (All_Email.url="*.zip*" OR All_Email.url="*.rar*" OR All_Email.url="*download*" OR All_Email.url="*uc?id=*") by All_Email.recipient All_Email.src_user All_Email.subject All_Email.url | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
[LLM] GREYVIBE PhantomRelayV1 watchdog persistence via Run key or scheduled task Installation Medium
Detects the PhantomRelayV1 'custom watchdog' persistence pattern — a paired powershell.exe process that immediately re-spawns a sibling powershell.exe within seconds of termination, registered via a Run/RunOnce key or a scheduled task. This is GREYVIBE's documented mechanism to keep the PowerShell RAT alive across reboots and termination. Rationale: Article calls out PhantomRelayV1's 'custom watchdog persistence mechanism' and kill-chain phase 3 specifies Run/RunOnce keys plus paired sibling re-spawn within seconds. The combination of Run-key registration of a hidden-window powershell + a 5-minute window with ≥2 sibling powershell spawns from a parent powershell is the watchdog fingerprint. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1547/001/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
ATT&CKT1547.001 T1053.005 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry Endpoint.Processes
let RunKeyPersist = DeviceRegistryEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
    | where RegistryKey has_any (@"\CurrentVersion\Run",@"\CurrentVersion\RunOnce")
    | where RegistryValueData has_any ("powershell","pwsh")
    | where RegistryValueData has_any ("-W Hidden","-WindowStyle Hidden","-EncodedCommand","-enc ","hidden","Start-Job","-NoP","-NonI")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData, InitiatingProcessFileName;
let WatchdogSpawn = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
    | where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Start-Job","Start-Process","-WindowStyle Hidden","While","watchdog")
    | summarize Spawns=count(), arg_min(Timestamp,*) by DeviceName, AccountName, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
    | where Spawns >= 2;
RunKeyPersist
| join kind=leftouter (WatchdogSpawn | project DeviceName, WatchdogTime=Timestamp, Spawns) on DeviceName
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData, WatchdogTime, Spawns
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where RegistryKey has_any ("\\CurrentVersion\\Run","\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnce")
| where RegistryValueData has_any ("powershell","pwsh")
| where RegistryValueData has_any ("-W Hidden","-WindowStyle Hidden","-EncodedCommand","-enc ","hidden","Start-Job","-NoP","-NonI","watchdog")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName
| join kind=leftouter (
    ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Start-Job","Start-Process","-WindowStyle Hidden","watchdog")
    | summarize Spawns=count(), WatchdogTime=min(TimeGenerated) by DvcHostname, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
    | where Spawns >= 2
) on DvcHostname

[LLM] GREYVIBE LegionRelay browser, Telegram and WhatsApp data harvest Actions on Objectives High
Hunts LegionRelay's credential and messenger data theft by alerting on powershell.exe (or unsigned binaries) opening Chrome/Edge/Firefox 'Login Data' and 'Cookies' SQLite files, %AppData%\Telegram Desktop\tdata, and WhatsApp local storage. These exact targets are listed in the article as LegionRelay capabilities. Rationale: Article lists LegionRelay capabilities verbatim: 'browser data theft, Telegram and WhatsApp data exfiltration', and kill-chain phase 6 specifies Chrome/Edge/Firefox 'Login Data' + 'Cookies' SQLite + tdata + WhatsApp local storage as the file targets. Combined with non-browser proc reading those paths, this is high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
ATT&CKT1555.003 T1539 T1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
   or FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",@"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",@"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\",@"\Telegram Desktop\tdata\",@"\WhatsApp\")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",@"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",@"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\",@"\Telegram Desktop\tdata\",@"\WhatsApp\")
   or FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","key4.db","key3.db")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","cmd.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName == ""
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","telegram.exe","whatsapp.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let TargetPaths = dynamic(["\\Google\\Chrome\\User Data\\","\\Microsoft\\Edge\\User Data\\","\\Mozilla\\Firefox\\Profiles\\","\\Telegram Desktop\\tdata\\","\\WhatsApp\\"]);
let TargetFiles = dynamic(["Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","key4.db","key3.db"]);
let LegitBrowserProcs = dynamic(["chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","telegram.exe","whatsapp.exe"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFilePath has_any (TargetPaths) or TargetFileName in~ (TargetFiles)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","cmd.exe")
| where not (ActingProcessName has_any (LegitBrowserProcs))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, Hash

[LLM] GREYVIBE DroneLink WireGuard tunnel install on user workstation Command & Control High
Detects DroneLink chain installing a WireGuard tunnel (wireguard.exe / wg.exe / tunnel.dll service) on a user workstation — the article cites fake Ukrainian-Armed-Forces charity sites delivering WireGuard and LegionRelay. Workstations almost never legitimately install ad-hoc WireGuard interfaces. Rationale: Article specifies DroneLink delivers WireGuard plus LegionRelay via charity-impersonation sites; kill-chain phase 8 calls out WireGuard tunnels from user endpoints as a high-fidelity C2 signal. Workstations rarely legitimately receive ad-hoc WireGuard installs, and excluding MSI/Intune/SCCM parents removes the corporate VPN deployment baseline. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1572/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1219/
ATT&CKT1572 T1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let WgProcs = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where FileName in~ ("wireguard.exe","wg.exe","wg-quick.exe")
       or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("WireGuard","tunnel.dll","/installtunnelservice","wg-quick")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msiexec.exe","setup.exe","intunemanagementextension.exe","ccmexec.exe")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256;
let WgFiles = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where FileName in~ ("wireguard.exe","wg.exe","tunnel.dll") or FolderPath has @"\WireGuard\"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
union WgProcs, WgFiles
| order by Timestamp desc
let WgFileNames = dynamic(["wireguard.exe","wg.exe","wg-quick.exe","tunnel.dll"]);
let ShellProcs = dynamic(["powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe"]);
let WgProcs = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where ActingProcessName has_any (WgFileNames)
        or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("WireGuard","tunnel.dll","/installtunnelservice","wg-quick")
    | where not (ParentProcessName has_any ("msiexec.exe","setup.exe","intunemanagementextension.exe","ccmexec.exe"))
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName;
let WgFiles = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where TargetFileName has_any (WgFileNames) or TargetFilePath has "\\WireGuard\\"
    | where ActingProcessName has_any (ShellProcs)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName;
WgProcs
| union WgFiles
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] GREYVIBE network egress to known C2 IP infrastructure Command & Control High
Alerts on any outbound connection from an endpoint to the 8 GREYVIBE C2 IPs documented in the WithSecure write-up. These IPs were used for PhantomRelay/LegionRelay beaconing and file exfiltration; any hit warrants immediate triage. Rationale: All 8 IPs are pulled verbatim from the IOC bundle in the kill-chain reconstruction and named as PhantomRelay/LegionRelay C2/exfil infrastructure (phases 8-9). Any organisational endpoint touching any of these IPs is a direct article-grounded IOC hit. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
let C2 = dynamic(["188.124.59.120","193.233.23.81","89.37.185.60","74.112.102.120","194.87.128.243","194.87.108.110","89.125.189.118","89.125.189.85"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (C2)
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Conns=count(),
            Procs=make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 10),
            Cmds=make_set(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, 10),
            Ports=make_set(RemotePort, 10)
            by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP
| order by FirstSeen asc
let C2 = dynamic(["188.124.59.120","193.233.23.81","89.37.185.60","74.112.102.120","194.87.128.243","194.87.108.110","89.125.189.118","89.125.189.85"]);
let FromCSL = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DestinationIP in (C2)
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, DeviceProduct, SentBytes, ReceivedBytes;
let FromAsim = ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DstIpAddr in (C2)
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkBytes;
FromCSL
| union FromAsim
| order by TimeGenerated asc

[LLM] GREYVIBE LegionRelay RDP enablement and outbound 3389 from user endpoint Command & Control High
Detects LegionRelay's RDP-access-setup behaviour: registry change enabling Terminal Services (fDenyTSConnections=0) and/or firewall rule allowing RDP, followed by outbound TCP/3389 from a workstation that normally does not initiate RDP. Article explicitly lists 'RDP access setup' as a LegionRelay capability. Rationale: Article calls out 'RDP access setup' as a LegionRelay capability; the standard mechanism is flipping fDenyTSConnections=0 plus a firewall allow rule. Pairing the registry change with a netsh/PowerShell firewall command in the same hour, on a workstation, is high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/001/
ATT&CKT1021.001 T1112 T1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry Endpoint.Processes
let RdpEnable = DeviceRegistryEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where (RegistryKey has @"\Terminal Server" and RegistryValueName =~ "fDenyTSConnections" and RegistryValueData == "0")
         or (RegistryKey has @"\WinStations\RDP-Tcp" and RegistryValueName =~ "UserAuthentication")
    | project RegTime=Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
let FwRule = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where (FileName =~ "netsh.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "Remote Desktop")
         or (FileName =~ "powershell.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Set-NetFirewallRule -DisplayGroup \"Remote Desktop\"","Enable-NetFirewallRule"))
    | project FwTime=Timestamp, DeviceName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName;
RdpEnable
| join kind=leftouter FwRule on DeviceName
| where isnull(FwTime) or FwTime between (RegTime - 1h .. RegTime + 1h)
| project RegTime, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueData, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FwTime, FwCmd=ProcessCommandLine
let RdpEnable = ImRegistryEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where (RegistryKey has "\\Terminal Server" and RegistryValue =~ "fDenyTSConnections" and RegistryValueData == "0")
         or (RegistryKey has "\\WinStations\\RDP-Tcp" and RegistryValue =~ "UserAuthentication")
    | project RegTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine;
let FwRule = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where (ActingProcessName has "netsh.exe" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "Remote Desktop")
         or (ActingProcessName has "powershell.exe" and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Set-NetFirewallRule","Enable-NetFirewallRule"))
    | project FwTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActingProcessCommandLine;
RdpEnable
| join kind=leftouter FwRule on DvcHostname
| where isnull(FwTime) or FwTime between (RegTime - 1h .. RegTime + 1h)

[LLM] GREYVIBE princess-club and Zoom/LAPAS lookalike domain access Reconnaissance High
Hunts inbound or outbound web traffic to the lure domains GREYVIBE used across PhantomClick, PrincessClub and Nebo: zoomconference.click/.app, lapas.live, strip-mens.tilda.ws, princess-mens.fun/.click/.com, princessclub.click. Captures both the initial-access click and any WebRTC AV-capture follow-on. Rationale: Article and IOC bundle name every one of these domains as lures used in PhantomClick (Zoom/LAPAS), PrincessClub (princess-* / strip-mens) and related chains. Any organisational endpoint resolving or visiting these is a direct article-grounded IOC hit; resolution covers the WebRTC-AV-capture flow as well. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/002/
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1583.001 T1204.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
let LureDomains = dynamic(["zoomconference.click","zoomconference.app","lapas.live","strip-mens.tilda.ws","princess-mens.fun","princess-mens-club.com","princess-mens.click","princessclub.click"]);
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any (LureDomains)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP;
let UrlHits = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where Url has_any (LureDomains)
    | project Timestamp, AccountUpn, Url, ActionType, IPAddress, IsClickedThrough;
NetHits
| union (UrlHits | extend DeviceName="<email-click>", InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountUpn, RemoteUrl=Url, RemoteIP=IPAddress)
| order by Timestamp desc
let LureDomains = dynamic(["zoomconference.click","zoomconference.app","lapas.live","strip-mens.tilda.ws","princess-mens.fun","princess-mens-club.com","princess-mens.click","princessclub.click"]);
let WebHits = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Url has_any (LureDomains) or HttpHostName has_any (LureDomains)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Url, HttpHostName;
let DnsHits = ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DnsQuery has_any (LureDomains)
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DnsQuery;
WebHits
| union DnsHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] GREYVIBE XMRig miner deployment on LegionRelay-infected host Actions on Objectives High
Detects XMRig command-line invocation (stratum+tcp, --donate-level, -o, --tls-fingerprint) on an endpoint, which the article notes GREYVIBE deploys on a subset of LegionRelay-infected machines for monetisation alongside espionage. The combination of mining-pool C2 strings on a normally-non-mining host is high-fidelity. Rationale: Article phase-10 detection hint specifies XMRig command-line flags (-o, --donate-level, stratum+tcp) and mining pool connections. These strings are mining-specific and almost never appear in legitimate enterprise software on a user workstation. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1496/ • https://github.com/xmrig/xmrig
ATT&CKT1496
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("stratum+tcp","stratum+ssl","--donate-level","--randomx","-o pool.","--tls-fingerprint","xmrig")
   or FileName =~ "xmrig.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("stratum+tcp","stratum+ssl","--donate-level","--randomx","-o pool.","--tls-fingerprint","xmrig")
   or ActingProcessName =~ "xmrig.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, SHA256

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count

     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent

    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId

title: Remote-Management (RMM) Tool Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0c
status: experimental
description: |
    AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera / Splashtop /
    RustDesk — RMM tools attackers commonly install for hands-on-
    keyboard access. Filter against the IT estate's known tool.
references:

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1219
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\AnyDesk.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer_Service.exe'
            - '\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe'
            - '\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe'
            - '\atera_agent.exe'
            - '\SplashtopStreamer.exe'
            - '\RustDesk.exe'

ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")

    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine

// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"

   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
